newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan urges power firms to raise utilisation rates.
newsitem.headline: Japan urges power firms to raise utilisation rates.

text.p: Japan's Trade Ministry said in an action programme unveiled on Thursday that improving electric power plants' capacity utilisation rates would help the utilities industry reduce electricity rates.
The action programme, due to be approved by the cabinet on Friday, addresses structural reform issues in a wide range of industries including telecommunications and distribution.
A large part of the plan, however, focuses on steps to promote competition in the power industry and slash electricity rates.
The action programme also called for the expansion of the independent power producer (IPP) scheme, which was first introduced in Japan in fiscal 1996/97.
The Japanese government pledged last year that it would bring Japan's high electricity rates down to levels comparable to overseas rates by 2001.

Government officials have declined to elaborate on the scale of rate reduction they seek. The average Japanese family pays about 20 percent more for its electricity, for example, than its German counterpart.

The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said in the action programme that Japan's 10 private utility companies would together be able to cut electricity costs by one percent, or about 150 billion yen, if it improved the industry's capacity utilisation rate by one percent.
The action programme said targets to improve the capacity utilisation rate, or load factor, would be set by the end of 1997.
Japan's power utilities' load factor has fallen to about 55 percent from 70 percent in the early 1970s, MITI said.
It also said the government would ask the electric utilities to set goals for buying electricity through the IPP scheme before the end of March 1998.
The action programme said it would review Japan's current system of generating and distributing electricity, which is dominated by 10 private electric power companies that enjoy regional monopolies.
The government hopes that expansion of the IPP scheme will stir competition in the industry.

In the first year of the IPP scheme, however, Japan's electric power companies awarded tenders to independent producers amounting to only about three million kilowatts (kw), a tiny proportion of the 775.4 billion kilowatt hours (kWh) consumed in 1996.
The action programme said electricity rates should be cut at an early date in 1998. It urged the industry to cut rates further in the year 2000.

Industry giant Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) and most other power utilities have already said they planned to lower electricity rates in 1998, although they did not provide a specific time frame.
